tagline: Up the Connecticut's east bank through a shipbuilders' village.
intro: The last mile and a half of Route 151 runs as Middle Haddam Road up the east bank of the Connecticut River, through the village of Middle Haddam, and ends at Route 66 in Cobalt. The village keeps to the shape of the ground, the river on one side and steep banks or stream valleys on the other.

Middle Haddam had a sawmill on Mill Brook and a ferry across the river early on, and by the Revolution it was trading with the West Indies and the coast and building ocean-going ships in its yards. Most of its 58 old buildings went up before 1835, and the Federal look has held.

moments.title: Middle Haddam
moments.text: Christ Episcopal Church of 1786 still stands among houses as old as 1732, and the village's lone Queen Anne Victorian is a summer house down by the town landing.

moments.title: Dart Island State Park
moments.text: A shad fishermen's sandbar, reached only by boat, given to the state in 1918 at about an acre and a half, billed in 1924 as the nation's smallest state park, officially 19 acres today.
